notes.title: AI App Generator
notes.text:
# AI App Generator

Flagship personal AI project built in 2026.
Users describe an app in chat; a multi-agent system writes, executes and iterates on full Next.js apps inside cloud sandboxes with live previews - like a focused v0 or bolt.new.

## Multi-agent pipeline

- Mastra: a coding agent plus fragment-title and response agents, driven by a 4-step typed workflow (sandbox acquire, history retrieval, agent execution, persistence and preview URL) with Zod-validated step contracts.
- Up to 50 tool-calling steps per task; custom tools (terminal, createOrUpdateFiles, readFiles, createSandbox) with strict Zod I/O schemas and runtime-context injection.

## Sandboxed execution

- E2B sandbox lifecycle management: reconnects to live sandboxes across user turns; restores project files from PostgreSQL into fresh sandboxes on expiry; custom Docker-based Next.js sandbox template (e2b.Dockerfile plus build script).

## Memory and observability

- Long-term agent memory with semantic recall (FastEmbed embeddings in LibSQL Vector), working memory, and auto-titled threads.
- AI tracing via Mastra observability exporters and structured Pino logging.

## SaaS platform and streaming UX

- tRPC end-to-end types, Drizzle ORM on PostgreSQL, Better Auth, Polar metered billing, per-user rate limiting and usage quotas.
- Vercel AI SDK v5 and AI Elements: streaming markdown (Streamdown), Shiki code views, live sandbox preview panel, generative charts.

## Deliberate stack iterations

- Clerk to Better Auth, Prisma to Drizzle, Inngest to Mastra, billing to Polar — each swap chosen deliberately, with a trade-off story to tell.

## Connects

- Skills: [[AI & LLM Engineering]], [[Full-Stack Development]].
- Tech: [[Mastra]], [[E2B Sandboxes]], [[Vercel AI SDK]], [[tRPC]], [[TypeScript]], [[Next.js]], [[React]], [[Databases]], [[Docker]].

notes.title: AI Oncology Capstone
notes.text:
# AI Oncology Capstone

AI-assisted breast cancer early-detection and diagnostics module designed for the COSMIC EHR in the Sri Lankan context, done in the Cambio context.
A full research to synthesis to ideation to POC design sprint, aligned to Cambio's roadmap and the EU Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI.

- Breast cancer pathways: types, staging, BI-RADS categories, mammography, ultrasound, MRI, biopsy; Sri Lankan context of about 17,000 new cases per year and under 20% screening uptake.
- EHR usability: physicians spend about 2 hours on EHR work per 1 hour of patient face-time; identified COSMIC Overview gaps (scattered widgets, lab request/result date disconnects) that fragment the patient snapshot during diagnosis.
- Lab utilization: 20-40% of tests unnecessary; false-positive risk scaling with test volume; "vein-to-brain" turnaround time framed as decision-support targets.

## Concept selection and requirements

- Evaluated three concepts (patient follow-up app, CNN image-classification clinician assistant, criteria/text-based risk model) through a weighted Harris Profile and selected the CNN assistant.
- Defined measurable AI requirements: SaaS detection model at 80%+ accuracy, 60% faster lab-investigation selection, 70%+ follow-up mammogram adherence, 5 minutes or less screen time per 20-minute consultation.

## Responsible AI and platform thinking

- Applied the EU Trustworthy AI guidelines (human oversight, robustness, privacy, transparency, fairness, accountability) as design constraints; designed clinician-in-the-loop second opinions that discourage over-requisitioning invasive tests.
- Proposed an anonymized central scan-image repository for internal and licensed third-party AI development; explored pharmacogenomics and CPIC precision medicine as a future layer.

## Process

- Stakeholder matrix, personas, journey maps, "How Might We" synthesis (reactive to proactive healthcare), cognitive systems engineering (decision-centered design, naturalistic decision-making), activity and information models, and requirements traceability from business to system requirements.

## Connects

- Skills: [[Healthcare Informatics]], [[AI & LLM Engineering]], [[Product Management & Business Analysis]].
- Roots: [[Cambio Software Engineering]], [[Healthcare Domain]].

notes.title: ELUX Travels
notes.text:
# ELUX Travels

Production multi-region travel booking platform (tours, hotels, flights, cruises) serving UK and Sri Lankan customers, live at eluxtravels.uk.
Built and shipped end to end by Arshaq - implementation, architecture and product engineering - with UI/visual design by Irfan Faiz: about 46,000 lines of hand-written TypeScript, 23 routes, 22 CMS collections, 42 server actions, 460+ commits over an 11-month build.

## Architecture

- TypeScript pnpm plus Turborepo monorepo: Next.js App Router frontend plus Payload CMS 3 headless backend, both running as Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext.
- Edge ISR: R2 incremental cache, D1 tag cache, Durable Object cache queue.
- Cross-service cache invalidation: Payload lifecycle hooks fire signed, secret-bearer revalidate requests that purge granular cache tags, so CMS edits hit the public site within seconds.
- Production data migrated from Neon Postgres to Cloudflare D1 via chunked replay scripts with foreign-key handling; 15 versioned migrations, 9 seed modules.

## Product

- End-to-end sales workflow: faceted multi-type travel search, enquiry intake for 4 request types, and a block-based quote and itinerary builder (hotel, flight, cruise and transport blocks composed into a branded quote document with its own preview site).
- Auth-gated customer dashboard unifying bookings, enquiries, quotes, payments and wishlist in a single trip timeline.

## Security and multi-region

- Google and Apple Sign-In via OAuth 2.0, including Apple form_post response mode and signed client-secret JWTs; httpOnly session cookies; 5-role RBAC with field- and collection-level access control.
- TLD-driven edge middleware routes .uk to GBP/GB and .lk to LKR/LK: 5 currencies (USD, GBP, LKR, EUR, AUD) from one codebase with no client-side currency flashing.

## Media, email and quality

- Google Places API enrichment mirrored into R2 media storage; images served through Cloudflare Image Resizing via a custom next/image loader.
- Transactional email flows (templated HTML) for enquiry and quote confirmations, plus email verification and password resets with time-limited tokens.
- Vitest integration tests against the Payload local API and Playwright e2e smoke tests; shared ESLint 9 flat config, Prettier and typecheck in the Turborepo pipeline.

## Connects

- Skills: [[Full-Stack Development]], [[Cloud & Edge Infrastructure]].
- Domain: [[Travel Tech]].
- Tech: [[Next.js]], [[React]], [[TypeScript]], [[Payload CMS]], [[Cloudflare Platform]], [[Databases]].
- The 0-to-production solo proof behind the founding-engineer and product stories.

notes.title: Snap
notes.text:
# Snap

Multi-tenant SaaS for photographers, live at snaphq.app (repo: webcules-inc/apps/snap). A studio runs its whole business in it - leads inbox, bookings with client-facing booking pages, calendar, projects, client galleries, invoices, contracts - on its own domain. Launched to production 2026-09-29 (v0.1.0); 18 tagged releases through v0.11.x.

## Platform shape

- vinext (Next.js App Router on [[Cloudflare Platform]] Workers), D1 as the system of record, R2 for gallery media, Better Auth (multi-tenant, 2FA), live [[Stripe]] billing, Drizzle.
- Plan tiers (Free/Lite/Studio) with server-enforced gates - template tiers, watermark lock, gallery layouts - and pricing invariant tests pinning what each tier gets.
- Scale (codebase-verified): about 93k LOC including tests (78k app code), 60+ D1 migrations, 12 Playwright e2e specs, 269 monorepo commits.

## Payments - Stripe Connect

- Client charges run **directly on the studio's own Stripe account** - Snap never holds client money or pays Stripe fees. Connected-account OAuth onboarding, a Connect-scoped webhook endpoint, per-studio currency.

## Custom domains - Cloudflare for SaaS

- Studios map their own domains: custom hostnames API, ORIGINLESS fallback origin, one workers route per active hostname re-ensured at deploy time, HTTP DCV, host resolution from x-forwarded-host. Verified live in production. Deploys refuse to move domains onto a worker missing secrets.

## Galleries and product surface

- R2 presigned uploads, streamed ZIP download-all at any size on every plan, photo-arrangement workspace, welcome collage; a Template Studio (gallery design schema v2, sectioned renderer, tier-gated server-side) with ComfyUI-generated sample imagery and self-hosted fonts.
- Contracts with e-signature (pdf-lib), QR-coded /b/ booking pages, Tiptap rich text, signup onboarding.

## Communications

- Inbox with threads and per-thread reply addresses, triage, snooze, keymap; inbound and outbound email on Cloudflare Email Service; a daily-status cron Worker; zero third-party analytics on client surfaces.

## Operating discipline

- Staging-first deploys with mandatory browser verification (`--staging-verified` gate), typecheck as a deploy blocker, rollback-first incident response - the policy written after the 2026-09-30 production outage.
- Docs are part of the feature: a Linear-style public docs section authored from the code, verified on staging, with real screenshots; commit messages written as release notes; a docs-guard agent team (coder, verifier, shooter) audits every release.
- Security audit cycle: 5 P0 + 12 P1 findings fixed with live P0 probes and role-gate source scans.

## Connects

- Skills: [[Full-Stack Development]], [[Cloud & Edge Infrastructure]], [[Product Management & Business Analysis]].
- Tech: [[Cloudflare Platform]], [[Stripe]], [[Next.js]], [[React]], [[Databases]], [[TypeScript]].
- Same era: [[tru]]. Earlier solo SaaS proof: [[ELUX Travels]].

notes.title: tru
notes.text:
# tru

Workflow-automation platform in the Tines/Zapier category, built natively on the [[Cloudflare Platform]] edge stack and priced per run - pay for executions, not seats (repo: arshaqsoul/tru). Build a workflow visually, test it, publish it, trust it ran. 269 commits, ~41k LOC TypeScript, 67 D1 migrations, and a decision log of 41 numbered architecture decisions with recorded reconsiderations.

## Execution engine

- Custom orchestrator on Durable Objects + Queues (build loop vs run loop); a graph execution model with conditional branching, bounded loops, parallel steps, sub-workflows, per-step retry policies, continue-on-error, response-body error detection, HTTP pagination and output caps.
- Run watchdog with terminal-state guards, whole-workflow dry-run through the real engine, draft/publish with immutable versions, per-step run history with guided recovery.
- CodeAction sandbox: Workers isolation plus application guardrails - the security spike modeled 26 attack patterns with sub-500ms cold starts.

## AI copilot (Jev)

- "Jev decides, the LLM generates": a typed control plane decides workflow structure and fields; the model generates within those rails. Confirm-then-act tool-calling harness running in a Worker via Cloudflare AI Gateway (BYOK).
- The app generator emits real code - generated in an alarm-driven Durable Object, bundled by a dedicated esbuild Worker, hosted from R2.
- Eval-first: a probe Worker runs decision, reshape and route eval suites - measure generation quality on real data before shipping. The typed per-app action catalog was built, evaluated and reverted on eval evidence (D022).

## Connectors and security

- Descriptor-driven integration catalog of 100+ providers (vendored ActivePieces pieces executing in-worker through a compatibility shim, D041): credentials as data, OAuth only where required, credential tiering - platform app / bring-your-own app / manual paste (D033). Plus external databases over TLS (Postgres, Supabase), Slack, email, webhook and HTTP connectors; a Make importer.
- Security posture: SSRF guard on the HTTP connector, tenant egress allowlists, one egress guard for every credentialed outbound fetch, MCP authorization compliance, a closed client-secret leak, RBAC and an audit log.

## Metering, billing and product

- Better Auth swapped in over the hand-rolled implementation (D007); projects/teams multi-tenancy; OpenAPI 3.1 + Scalar docs served by the Worker; WebSocket-hibernation team presence; pages, records, cases and dashboards surface ops use cases.
- Proven through three UAT rounds with bug-fix loops; landing page with animated product demos, bento grid and a live pricing calculator. Staging-stage, pre-production.

## Connects

- Skills: [[AI & LLM Engineering]], [[Cloud & Edge Infrastructure]], [[Full-Stack Development]], [[Product Management & Business Analysis]].
- Tech: [[Cloudflare Platform]], [[Databases]], [[TypeScript]].
- Deliberate-decision stories double as interview material; sibling production SaaS: [[Snap]]; adjacent webcules projects: [[webcules-init]], [[AI App Generator]].

notes.title: Villvay Search Platform
notes.text:
# Villvay Search Platform

Multi-tenant B2B e-commerce search platform for Wurth companies (Wurth Baer Supply, Wurth LaCrosse), built at [[Villvay Systems]].
About 35,000 lines of TypeScript and Python across a Turborepo monorepo, with 5 tenants times environments isolated end to end.

## Search relevance (the headline)

- 16-layer progressive cascade: exact SKU, phrase slop tiers, exact word, edge n-gram and n-gram, combined-fields, fuzzy, with high-precision tiers suppressing lower tiers at result thresholds.
- Weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion across 11 retrievers with per-retriever weights, rank windows, rank constants, curation boosts and query rules.
- ELSER sparse-vector semantic fallback computed at ingest through an inference pipeline, so query-time inference latency is zero.
- E-commerce linguistics: unit-of-measure synonym expansion ("5mm" matches "5 millimeter"), fraction and dimension normalization, SKU punctuation-stripping analyzers (10 analyzers, 11 character filters, 16 index definitions), attribute-to-natural-language transforms, per-account part numbers via nested account-filtered queries, and barcode lookup as a dedicated route.

## Search API and edge architecture

- Zero-dependency TypeScript Cloudflare Worker compiling Elasticsearch query DSL by hand over fetch/NDJSON.
- Two-phase retrieval: rank IDs via _msearch, fetch only the final page via _mget.
- Config-driven behavior: 11 routes, 10 search collections per tenant, 3-level base/tenant/environment YAML merge - onboarding a tenant requires configuration only, zero code.
- Disjunctive faceting with post-filtering so facet counts reflect unfiltered distributions; strict-match detection for single precise hits.

## Data engineering

- Airflow (CeleryExecutor): one templated DAG generating per-tenant DAGs (6 pipelines x products, categories, brands), dynamic task mapping fanning out batches for parallelism and failure isolation.
- 4-hour incremental syncs with 24-hour watermarks and idempotent streaming_bulk upserts; Redis as the staged batch store.
- Registry-pattern source connectors: paginated REST APIs plus Selenium/Chromium site crawls.
- Declarative per-tenant YAML transformation engine (10+ operations: cast, field mapping, HTML decode, combination, attribute stringification, boost-score computation).

## Configuration platform and admin dashboard

- Configuration API: 33 tRPC procedures across 6 routers, Auth0 JWTs carrying tenant and environment claims, draft to preview to promote flows, calendar versioning, config diffing, one-click rollback, R2 audit trails, and preview deployments triggered by dispatching its own GitHub Actions workflow.
- Next.js 15 dashboard: 8 pages, 18 typed React Query hooks, drag-and-drop layer ordering, synonyms manager with CSV import/export, index and mapping management with document preview, live search preview console.
- Types and validators generated from 9 JSON Schemas so configuration, API and dashboard forms stay in lockstep.

## Analytics loop

- Event-collector worker indexes click and search events that power autocomplete suggestions and trending searches.
- Per-query telemetry (layer breakdown, fallback usage, strict-match detection, latency) streams via ctx.waitUntil into Cloudflare Queues and a batched bulk consumer, off the request path.

## Delivery

- 4 parameterized GitHub Actions deploy workflows (dev to QA to prod promotion), secrets pulled from Cloudflare KV at deploy time, SSH self-hosted-runner deploys.
- Docker Compose Airflow stack (9 services including a custom Chromium/Selenium image).

## Connects

- Skills: [[Search & Relevance Engineering]], [[Data Engineering]], [[Cloud & Edge Infrastructure]], [[Full-Stack Development]].
- Domain: [[E-commerce & B2B]].
- Tech: [[Elasticsearch]], [[Apache Airflow]], [[Cloudflare Platform]], [[Next.js]], [[React]], [[TypeScript]], [[Python]], [[tRPC]], [[Databases]], [[Docker]].

# AI & LLM Engineering

Hands-on LLM agent engineering: multi-agent orchestration, tool calling with strict schemas, sandboxed execution, agent memory, and streaming AI UX.

## In practice

- Multi-agent orchestration in [[Mastra]]: specialized agents, typed workflows, runtime context injection - proven in the [[AI App Generator]].
- Tool and function calling with Zod-validated I/O contracts; ReAct-style loops of up to 50 steps.
- Sandboxed code execution on [[E2B Sandboxes]] with state that survives restarts.
- Agent memory: semantic recall with FastEmbed embeddings in a LibSQL vector store, working memory, thread management.
- AI observability: distributed tracing (Mastra exporters) and structured logging.
- Streaming UX: [[Vercel AI SDK]] v5, AI Elements, Streamdown, generative UI.
- LLM APIs: OpenAI, Hugging Face, Google Vertex; prompt engineering for code-generation agents and structured output extraction.
- POC tooling: v0, bolt.new, Claude Code; daily work in MCP-based agent tooling (custom agents and skills).
- Eval-first LLM features: decision, reshape and route eval suites in a probe Worker - measure generation quality on real data before shipping; one feature (the typed action catalog) was built, evaluated and reverted on eval evidence.
- App generation as production infrastructure: an alarm-driven Durable Object generates real code, a dedicated esbuild Worker bundles it, R2 hosts it ([[tru]]).
- Retrieval bridge: the search relevance work (ELSER, RRF) is retrieval engineering — half of RAG — and semantic recall over a vector store covers the other half.

# Cloud & Edge Infrastructure

Cloudflare-first edge architecture and pragmatic delivery pipelines.

- Durable Objects as the stateful substrate: [[tru]]'s workflow orchestrator (build loop vs run loop), alarm-driven app generation, WebSocket-hibernation team presence; the cache queue on the search platform.
- Cloudflare for SaaS custom hostnames: per-customer domains on an ORIGINLESS fallback origin, one workers route per active hostname re-ensured at deploy time, HTTP DCV - verified in production ([[Snap]]).
- Email on the edge: inbound and outbound via Cloudflare Email Service, with a dedicated email-router Worker ([[tru]]) and per-thread reply addresses ([[Snap]]).
- Staging-first delivery discipline: deploy scripts that refuse production without a browser-verified staging pass, typecheck gates, version-pinned rollback as the first incident response ([[Snap]]).
- OpenNext adapter to run Next.js at the edge with ISR (R2 incremental cache, D1 tag cache, Durable Object cache queue).
- Multi-tenant isolation: tenant-prefixed indices, per-tenant YAML merged at build time, per-tenant Workers, tenant and environment claims enforced in auth.
- GitHub Actions delivery: 4 parameterized deploy workflows with dev to QA to prod promotion, secrets pulled from Cloudflare KV at deploy time, SSH self-hosted runners, and preview deployments dispatched from an API.
- Docker Compose stacks: a 9-service Airflow deployment including a custom Chromium/Selenium image - see [[Docker]].

notes.title: Data Engineering

# Data Engineering

Batch ETL, incremental sync, and data-quality work - from Airflow DAGs to bank data migrations.

## In practice

- [[Apache Airflow]] (CeleryExecutor): templated DAGs generating per-tenant pipelines, dynamic task mapping for parallelism and failure isolation.

notes.title: Search & Relevance Engineering
notes.text:
# Search & Relevance Engineering

Production search for industrial B2B catalogs: layered relevance, semantic fallback, and a closed behavioral analytics loop.

## In practice

- [[Elasticsearch]] 8 on Elastic Cloud: query DSL, index mapping and analyzer design, aggregations and disjunctive faceting, relevance tuning.
- 16-layer progressive cascade from exact SKU to fuzzy, with tier suppression once minimum result thresholds are met.
- Weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion across 11 retrievers, avoiding the score-normalization problems of naive blending.
- ELSER sparse-vector semantic search computed at ingest through an inference pipeline, so the hot path pays no query-time inference.
- E-commerce linguistics: unit-of-measure synonyms, fraction and dimension normalization, SKU punctuation-stripping analyzers, attribute-to-natural-language transforms, per-account part numbers, barcode routes.
- Two-phase retrieval: _msearch ranks IDs, _mget fetches only the final page.
- Behavioral loop: edge-collected clicks and searches become next week's autocomplete suggestions and trending searches.

## Where it shows up

- [[Villvay Search Platform]] at [[Villvay Systems]].
- Bridge to AI retrieval: [[AI & LLM Engineering]].

notes.title: Stripe
notes.text:
# Stripe

Production billing on [[Snap]] - Checkout, subscriptions and Connect.

- Direct charges via Connect: client payments run on the studio's own Stripe account, so Snap never holds client money or pays Stripe fees. Destination charges were spiked and rejected - they debit the platform - and direct charges are blocked for legacy Express accounts on new platforms, which shaped the onboarding flow.
- Studios connect an existing Stripe account through OAuth; a second webhook endpoint scoped to Connected accounts handles events arriving on studios' own accounts (separate signing secret from the platform webhook).
- Plan prices are auto-created from plan metadata on first checkout - verified in live mode ($15/mo Lite). Charges follow the studio's currency; a studio is bookable once its Connect charges are enabled, even while identity verification or payouts are still pending.
- Live/test discipline: live keys + live webhook in production since the 2026-09-29 launch; test keys + the 4242 card on staging. Voiding an invoice deactivates its payment link on the studio account.

Skill: [[Full-Stack Development]]. Used in: [[Snap]]. Metered-billing alternative used on [[tru]] and the [[AI App Generator]]: Polar.
